title: Strip Out The AI-Driven ASP Inflation & 2026’s $1 Trillion Becomes $625 Billion
text:
Daniel Nenni
Founder
Staff member

Future Horizons’ October 2026 bulletin argues that the semiconductor industry’s extraordinary growth is being driven primarily by artificial intelligence infrastructure and rising average selling prices (ASPs), rather than a broad increase in chip demand. Its headline assessment suggests that removing AI-related price inflation would reduce the apparent 2026 market value from $1 trillion to approximately $625 billion.

According to the bulletin’s cited WSTS figures, August semiconductor sales increased 156.3% compared with August 2025. Sales adjusted for the five-week reporting month rose 23.3% month on month, versus 13.6% in the previous month. Integrated circuits accounted for most of the expansion, recording annual growth of 175.9%, while discretes and optoelectronics grew by only 8.4% and 9.2%, respectively.

The report describes current growth as unprecedented, exceeding earlier cyclical peaks of 59.3% in June 2000 and 66.6% in January 2010. It attributes the boom to confidence that AI will transform society and the global economy, encouraging hyperscalers to commit enormous sums to infrastructure.

However, author Malcolm Penn questions whether this investment provides a sustainable foundation for the wider semiconductor market. Unlike previous cycles, which were broadly supported by rising unit demand, the current expansion is concentrated in highly specialised AI infrastructure. Expensive AI chips also face affordability constraints in conventional applications that historically sustained the industry.

The bulletin accepts AI’s substantial long term potential, including new applications and eventual semiconductor demand. Its concern is the present imbalance between infrastructure spending and commercially meaningful end products, alongside dependence on inflated prices.

Penn therefore advises companies to benefit from current growth while avoiding assumptions that today’s exceptional expansion, particularly ASP increases, will continue indefinitely. Businesses should maintain contingency plans in case conditions weaken. The bulletin also promotes its full report, a November semiconductor awareness workshop, and a January 2027 industry update webinar for further analysis and education.
